text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-Prime Minister Hariri discussed with U.S. Vice President Al Gore in Washington the issue of lifting the travel ban on Lebanon. Hariri says another "Friends of Lebanon" conference will be held soon either in Washington or in Europe to follow the December 16 Washington meeting.
-Hariri will meet French President Chirac in Paris on Saturday.
-The Arab League's secretary-general says: "Israel's intransigence is behind the crisis in the region."
-A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon said at least one Katyusha rocket was fired from south Lebanon into Israel last week.
-An Israeli government minister proposes that Egyptian and Jordanian soldiers take over from Israeli troops in south Lebanon.

-The General Labour Confederation (CGTL) will continue to pressure the government "to correct its policies", CGTL chief Abu Rizk said. The CGTL has called for a general strike on November 29 to protest against the government's social and media policies.
-The multinational American Life Insurance Company says it will reopen its regional bureau in Beirut after a 12-year of closure.
-PM Hariri signed a $65 million loan agreement with the chairman of the World Bank in Washington.
